full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the plaintiff petitioners instituted Other Suit No.334 of 2004 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chakaria, Cox's Bazar praying for simple declaration of title over the suit land as more fully described in the schedule of the plaint impleading the defendant Nos.1-6. The action of Rezaul Karim the present respondent No.1 having cast clouds over the long possession of the suit land of the petitioners and as such, the petitioners are apprehended to get the preferential relief in respect of lease hold of shrimp khas land as per principle of present Government, moreover the present petitioners are very weak both by men and money with the strength of respondent No.1 and in view of the facts and circumstances made above to ensure transparency and accountability of the petitioners are necessary otherwise the petitioners will be deprived of their fundamental right and preferential relief and the petitioners are compelled to file this present suit praying for declaration of the title over the suit land. The petitioners are bonafide cultivators and particularly their mind to cultivate shrimp khas land which is the only means of their livelihood of families from their fore fathers and as such, the petitioners are genuine cultivators of shrimp by profession. One Anisul Haque was the original lease holder of the disputed shrimp khas land and in this connection a document was made between the original lease holder and the authority concerned but in fact the original lease holder was not shrimp cultivator by profession that is why Anisul Haque the original lessee executed a power of attorney on 30.01.2003 in favour of the petitioners who are fit for shrimp cultivation and in view of that an agreement was made between the parties. Having got the suit land the petitioners spent a lot of money for digging that for suitable shrimp cultivation of khas land in this respect the original lease holder has been benefited to end the met in consideration of money. Subsequently the lease was cancelled as the original lease holder failed to comply the lease money to the Government as per terms of the lease deed made between the parties and as such the present petitioners are actual physical possessors of the suit land applied for taking lease before Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Cox's Bazar and submitted all papers in support of their legitimate claims and the matter was referred to Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar through Thana Nirbahi Officer and this regard an enquiry was held and a reply was given by the authority concerned in favour of the petitioners. The authority concerned (Land) received lease money and huge amount of compensation money vide D.C.R. No.090451452 dated 22.11.2004 from year to year from the petitioners properly and recorded as possessors of the shrimp khas land. On 19.07.2004 the petitioners applied separately for taking lease of shrimp khas land measuring 0.5+0.5=0.10 acre of khas land before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Rev) Cox's Bazar on the ground of getting preferential relief and also actual possessors as shrimp cultivators by profession from their fore father. On 21.10.2004 Rezaul Karim son of Alhaj Delwar Hossain who resides far away from the suit land and he is not shrimp cultivator by profession, he is a Government service holder who is not competent to get lease of shrimp khas land measuring 0.10 acres of land as per present ruling of Government that Rezaul Karim only filed an application recommend by some influential persons of that locality for taking lease of shrimp khas land for the greater interest of vested quarter not for the purpose of own interest ignoring the actual facts and circumstances of the case and actual position of the suit land. 

 3. Mr. N.K. Saha, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division adopted wrong procedure by not giving the preferential relief to genuine shrimp cultivator though directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession in favour of plaintiff petitioner but the Government and their functionaries arc strictly directed to lease out the suit property at any suitable time in favour of the highest bidder ignoring the Government Nitimala and this error has vitiated the judgment that on 19.07.2004 Abul Hossain, Sabbir Ahmed, the present petitioners applied separately for taking lease of shrimp khas land measuring 0.5+0.5=0.10 acres of khas land before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Cox's Bazar on the ground of getting preferential relief and also actual possessors as shrimp cultivators by profession from their fore-father and this aspect ought to have advanced than the defendant respondent who applied for taking lease latter on 21.10.2004 as a Government service holder and as such this is not a defect into proceeding itself but material defects in substance of impugned judgment passed the High Court Division. The learned Advocate further submitted that the High Court Division upon an erroneous conception of law as well as of facts in discharging the Rule without any order as to cost without giving any direction for leasing out the suit property to genuine shrimp cultivator as a highest bidder as per present Government Nitimala; that since admittedly the plaintiff-petitioners acquired 0.10 acres of Government khas land by way of barga settlement from Anisul Haque the original lessee and Government accepted lease money vide D.C.R. No.0045452 dated 22.11.2004 and two applications praying for taking lease made by the petitioners are still pending before the authority concerned of the Government totally ignoring this aspects by not giving to lease out particularly to genuine shrimp cultivator as a highest bidder as per Government Nitimala and thus suffer from a patent illegality, legal infirmity and flagrant error of law warranting interference by this Court.
